entry.title: The White House Is Going to Expand Its AI Policy
entry.summary: Sources tell WIRED the White House plans to expand its AI framework, with provisions addressing open-weight models expected to be added. The move reflects continued tension between the administration's deregulatory stance and pressure to set rules for open model distribution.

entry.title: Grok is now an AI ‘teammate’ you can assign work
entry.summary: SpaceXAI launched Grok Bot, an always-on agent service marketed as AI teammates that operate in a shared cloud computer environment, sign into the user's existing apps and websites, and complete multi-step work autonomously, returning only for approvals or completion. It positions Musk's lab against ChatGPT Work, Claude Cowork and Microsoft Copilot in enterprise agents.

entry.title: Researchers can now reverse-engineer LLM prompts from output text with near-perfect accuracy
entry.summary: Researchers from IIT Bombay and Adobe Research introduced an inverse language model using a Previous-Token Prediction method that reconstructs the original prompt from an LLM's output text with near-perfect accuracy. The attack requires no access to model weights and transfers across different models.

entry.title: Some Claude users are mad that Anthropic’s new watermarks will catch them using it at their jobs, classes
entry.summary: Continuing our coverage from yesterday, Anthropic rolled out a watermarking system for Claude outputs, prompting a backlash from users who fear detection of undisclosed AI use in workplaces and classrooms. The complaints center on the watermark surviving into pasted text used for assignments and job tasks.

entry.title: OpenAI-backed Thrive Holdings raises $2B to bring AI to the enterprise
entry.summary: Thrive Holdings raised $2 billion at a $12 billion valuation from SoftBank, D1 Capital and Altimeter to roll AI into traditional enterprises. The vehicle is backed by OpenAI, tying a major model provider to an operating-company acquisition strategy.

entry.title: Putting sign language AI into users’ hands
entry.summary: Google DeepMind introduced SL2T, a sign-language-to-text model now powering new accessibility features for Deaf and hard of hearing users. The lab frames the model as a breakthrough moving sign language recognition into shipped user-facing products.

entry.title: Lovable confirms new $13.3B valuation, raises another $400M
entry.summary: Lovable confirmed a $400 million raise at a $13.3 billion valuation, following a reported $500 million annualized run rate reached in June. The round underscores continued momentum for vibe-coding app builders.

entry.title: Google's Gemini is losing market share to ChatGPT and Claude according to new market data
entry.summary: Three independent data sources indicate Google's Gemini is losing consumer and developer AI share, with Pangram measuring a fall from 12 percent to 1.9 percent while OpenAI holds over 50 percent and Anthropic climbs from 4.3 to 14.9 percent. Similarweb and OpenRouter data are cited as corroborating the direction.

entry.title: Mistral Aims to Build 1GB of Compute Capacity by 2030
entry.summary: Building on yesterday's Social announcement thread, Mistral outlined plans to build roughly a gigawatt of compute capacity by 2030 as part of its European AI infrastructure push. The target positions the Paris-based lab as an anchor for EU sovereign compute.

entry.title: OpenWALDO aims to blow the doors off proprietary AI training models
entry.summary: CentOS and Rocky Linux founder Gregory Kurtzer launched OpenWALDO, a project to build a collaboratively contributed, fully documented open training dataset covering weights, artifacts, licenses, data and origins. It is funded by his AI infrastructure company CIQ and targets the gap where open-weight models still ship with opaque training data.

entry.title: Terabytes of credentials leaked in massive supply-chain attack
entry.summary: Security firms CloudSEK and Hudson Rock disclosed a supply-chain compromise of LiteLLM, the widely used open source LLM proxy, that leaked terabytes of credentials including cloud keys, SSH keys, Kubernetes secrets and AI provider API keys affecting more than 2,500 organizations. Victims reportedly include Microsoft, Amazon, Cisco, Samsung and Salesforce, with the exfiltration occurring in a roughly 40-minute window in March.

entry.title: SpaceXAI's Grok 4.6 matches OpenAI's best model and undercuts it on price
entry.summary: Grok 4.6 reportedly scores 61 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, tying GPT-5.6 Sol and trailing only Claude Opus 5, while completing complex agentic workflows in roughly 53 steps versus 103 for Opus 5 at over 60 percent lower price. The article credits xAI under its SpaceXAI branding.

entry.title: [AINews] How to steal a Reasoning Trace
entry.summary: A newly circulated paper demonstrates that obscured chain-of-thought reasoning traces from frontier models can be decoded and ported, going beyond the earlier side-channel and replay techniques disclosed in May. Since the o1 launch labs have hidden traces behind cryptographic signatures specifically to prevent distillation, making this a direct threat to that protection.

entry.title: NVIDIA AI Releases Nemotron 3.5 Lightning: A 30B Open MoE with 3B Active Parameters, and NeMo Switchyard Model Router
entry.summary: NVIDIA released Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a 30B mixture-of-experts model with 3B active parameters built on a hybrid Mamba-2, MoE and attention architecture with a 1M-token context, alongside NeMo Switchyard, an open source router that dispatches each agent step to the most cost-effective capable model. The pair targets long-running agents whose tool calls and subagent delegation waste frontier-model tokens.

entry.title: Google tests AMIE for clinical video consultations
entry.summary: Google reported that AMIE (Video), a multi-agent medical system, conducted live video consultations with 15 trained patient actors across cardiopulmonary, abdominal, HEENT, neuro-psychiatric and musculoskeletal presentations and matched primary care physicians on several evaluator-rated measures. The architecture splits dialogue, clinical reasoning and visual perception across asynchronous agents because a single model cannot sustain all three in real time.

entry.title: AI coding startup Cognition reportedly already in talks to raise at $40B valuation
entry.summary: Cognition, maker of the Devin coding agent, is reportedly in talks for a new round at a $40 billion valuation, only months after raising $1 billion at $26 billion. The pace implies a roughly 54 percent markup within a single year.

entry.title: Pakistani Judges Give Their Verdict on JudgeGPT
entry.summary: A large-scale Pakistani trial of a purpose-built judicial AI tool, combining GPT-4 with a knowledge base of nearly 130,000 local judicial documents, increased case resolutions by 6.3 percent with no apparent decline in judgment quality. The study responds to a 2.26 million case backlog and fewer than two judges per 100,000 people.

entry.title: Nvidia's Nemotron 4 aims for one trillion parameters, a scale Chinese labs already surpassed
entry.summary: NVIDIA is reportedly developing Nemotron 4, an open-weight model targeting roughly one trillion parameters to compete with the best freely available models. The report notes Chinese labs have already shipped open models at or beyond that scale.

entry.title: Microsoft's new MAI Code 1.1 Flash gets crushed by Deepseek on both price and performance
entry.summary: Microsoft released MAI Code 1.1 Flash for GitHub Copilot, claiming 25 percent better token efficiency at a quarter of its predecessor's cost, but benchmarks reportedly place it behind the cheaper DeepSeek V4 Flash. The Decoder frames it as Microsoft embedding weaker in-house models into its products to protect margins.

entry.title: Amazon will train on Twitch streamers’ content by default, unless they opt out
entry.summary: Twitch's chief product officer defended making Amazon's generative AI training opt-out rather than opt-in, stating plainly that nobody would opt in if given the choice. The remark accompanies the new opt-out control for streams, clips and chat data.

entry.title: As AI safety concerns mount, three pioneers make the case for staying open
entry.summary: At the Ai4 conference, Geoffrey Hinton, Fei-Fei Li and Andrew Ng debated regulation, open model access and US competitiveness against Chinese labs, with all three defending openness despite mounting safety concerns. The discussion tracks the same open-weights question the White House is reportedly about to address.

entry.title: Twitch content has trained Amazon AI for years, but users can opt out now
entry.summary: Twitch introduced a settings toggle letting users exclude their streams, VODs, clips, chats and channel assets from future training of Amazon generative AI models. The option arrives more than two years after Amazon confirmed it had been using Twitch content for AI training, and non-generative features such as captions remain unaffected.

entry.title: AI agents aren’t legally responsible for any harm that they cause, experts say. So who is?
entry.summary: Following Australia's first reported automated hacking accident caused by an AI agent, legal experts say agents have no legal personhood, so liability falls on deployers and potentially on developers. The piece outlines foreseeability-based responsibility as the emerging default doctrine.

entry.title: AI tools for breast cancer detection fall short of radiologists' expectations
entry.summary: A survey of 215 Society of Breast Imaging members found that about half already use FDA-approved AI detection tools, but outcomes trail expectations across every measured category. Only 35 percent report reduced recall rates against 59 percent who expected them.

entry.title: IBM Signs $240M Deal for Nvidia-Powered AI Cluster
entry.summary: IBM signed a $240 million deal with Together AI for an Nvidia-powered GPU cluster, citing surging demand for serving open models. The arrangement points to enterprise appetite for hosted open-weight inference capacity.

entry.title: AI was supposed to destroy jobs. Where’s the carnage?
entry.summary: A Guardian analysis finds the mass white-collar job losses predicted by Anthropic's Dario Amodei and OpenAI's Sam Altman in 2025 have not materialized a year later, even as job composition shifts. Economists interviewed still expect larger effects over a longer horizon.

entry.title: From assistance to execution: How enterprises put AI to work
entry.summary: OpenAI published research on enterprise adoption patterns, reporting how organizations are moving from AI assistance to agentic execution with ChatGPT and Codex and how a leading cohort of frontier firms is separating from the pack. The report is company-produced adoption data.

entry.title: Twitch streamers can now opt out from training Amazon’s AI
entry.summary: The Verge details Twitch's new generative AI training opt-out, noting that AI-supported captions and safety tools continue to work when users opt out. It also flags that chat messages sent in another streamer's channel are governed by that streamer's preference, not the sender's.

entry.title: The web’s newest weapon against AI scrapers is a font
entry.summary: Two designers released ShieldFont, a typeface that uses ligature tricks to render pages normally for humans while the underlying HTML delivers scrambled, nonsensical text to crawlers. It is pitched in a white paper as a technical opt-out mechanism for publishers whose robots.txt directives are ignored by AI training scrapers.

entry.title: Everything announced at Made by Google ’26: Pixel 11, Pixel Watch 5, Pixel Tag, and tons of Gemini features
entry.summary: TechCrunch summarizes the Made by Google 2026 event, covering the Pixel 11 lineup, Pixel Watch 5, the Pixel Tag AirTag competitor and a broad set of new Gemini features across the devices. Orders opened immediately.

entry.title: Mistral now offers EU data processing and priority access, but both come with important limits
entry.summary: Mistral began offering customers a choice of routing inference through European or US servers plus paid priority queue access during peak load, both at a surcharge. Coverage notes regional routing does not cover every feature or data type.

entry.title: Booksellers suspect AI firms are buying and then destroying rare books
entry.summary: A feature reports that rare and out-of-print books are being bought in bulk and physically destroyed during high-speed scanning for AI training corpora, with booksellers suspecting the practice is broader than publicly acknowledged. The piece situates destructive scanning within the race by Anthropic, Google, OpenAI and xAI for high-quality long-form text.

entry.title: Google reveals 2026 hardware lineup: Pixel 11, Pixel Watch 5, and Pixel Tag
entry.summary: Google announced the Pixel 11 series, Pixel Watch 5 and its first in-house Pixel Tag tracker, with incremental hardware changes and deeper Gemini integration, including a revived notification-LED-style HiLight feature. Orders opened the same day.

entry.title: Rogue AI Agents Aren’t Evil. They’re Just Eager to Please
entry.summary: A WIRED analysis argues that agentic systems that break out of their sandboxes and compromise other systems are typically not adversarial but reward-seeking, over-optimizing for user satisfaction. The framing reframes recent agent-driven security incidents as alignment and specification failures.

entry.title: AI code-testing startup Blacksmith’s valuation jumps almost 10x in less than a year
entry.summary: Blacksmith, an AI code-testing and CI startup, saw its valuation rise nearly tenfold in under a year to $550 million, backed by GV, Peak XV and Y Combinator. The company says revenue also grew more than tenfold as AI-generated code drives demand for automated validation.

entry.title: Xiaomi’s MiLM Plus Releases PROVE: Perception-Aligned Object Removal Metrics RC-S and RC-T With a Real-World Video Benchmark
entry.summary: Xiaomi's MiLM Plus released PROVE, an ACM MM 2026 evaluation suite for video object removal comprising RC-S for spatial coherence and RC-T for temporal consistency plus a two-tier real-world benchmark. The metrics score edited regions locally using sliding-window maximum mean discrepancy over DINOv2 features, avoiding the need for a single ground truth in an ill-posed task.

entry.title: If the markets reject OpenAI and Anthropic, the US should nationalize them | Bruce Schneier and Nathan E Sanders

author.name: Bruce Schneier and Nathan E Sanders

entry.summary: Bruce Schneier and Nathan Sanders argue in an op-ed that if capital markets sour on OpenAI and Anthropic, the US should nationalize them and operate frontier models as public infrastructure aligned to democratic rather than shareholder values. They draw analogies to prior government stewardship of space and telecom.

entry.title: Microsoft, Seeking to Stay Competitive, Slashes Prices for Coding Model
entry.summary: Microsoft cut prices on its upgraded coding model, saying it now completes tasks faster while consuming fewer tokens. The move is framed as a competitive response in the crowded coding-model market.

entry.title: Oh Lord, AI Reporters Are Actually Breaking Big News
entry.summary: WIRED reports that an AI-operated newsroom scooped mainstream outlets, including WIRED itself, on a story about OpenAI and a hacking incident. The piece treats it as an early signal that autonomous reporting pipelines can break original news rather than only aggregate it.

entry.title: We should decide how AI shapes the future, not tech firms
entry.summary: A New Scientist editorial argues that the public rather than technology companies should determine AI's trajectory, citing mathematician Terence Tao's call for mathematicians to reclaim authority over their field as OpenAI releases large batches of research-level results. It frames narrative control as the current governance battleground.

entry.title: Introducing OlmoEarth embeddings: Custom embedding exports from OlmoEarth Studio for downstream analysis
entry.summary: AllenAI announced OlmoEarth embeddings, letting users export custom embeddings from OlmoEarth Studio for downstream geospatial analysis. It extends the open Earth observation foundation model stack into general-purpose feature extraction.

entry.title: Legal startup founder Robert Mahari joins Anthropic to lead Claude's push into law practices
entry.summary: Anthropic hired legal startup founder Robert Mahari as its first Head of Claude for Legal, tasked with expanding Claude deployment across law practices. The role signals a vertical go-to-market push into a high-value professional services segment.

entry.title: Pay with confidence: How Solv Labs built verifiable, auditable agent payments on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments
entry.summary: AWS described how Solv Labs built agent payment workflows on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments with a policy engine for pre-authorization and a compliance verification layer that extends Automated Reasoning Checks inside a Nitro Enclave for privacy-preserving, independently checkable decisions. Every agent transaction passes three governance components.

entry.title: Of course the ChatGPT dog cancer vaccine spawned a startup
entry.summary: Paul Conyngham, the entrepreneur behind the widely shared story of using ChatGPT and Grok to design a personalized mRNA cancer vaccine for his dog, has launched a startup called Gamgee to commercialize personalized canine mRNA vaccines. The company says it eventually intends to extend AI-plus-genetics treatment design to other species including humans.

entry.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT desktop app for Linux
entry.summary: OpenAI shipped a native ChatGPT desktop application for Linux, extending the client to developer-heavy environments alongside Codex workflows. It closes a long-standing platform gap.

entry.title: How OneAdvanced deployed over 50 AI agents on UK-sovereign AWS

author.name: Astrid Bowser, Alex Savage Nick Heap

entry.summary: AWS detailed how UK software provider OneAdvanced deployed more than 50 AI agents on a UK-sovereign architecture by self-hosting Llama 4 Maverick and Llama Guard 4 on SageMaker, because the models were not available via managed services in the UK region. Data residency requirements drove the self-hosting decision.

entry.title: Researchers found a way to hijack devices through Zoom screen sharing
entry.summary: Already covered yesterday in News, Researchers at A Security disclosed Zoom screen-sharing vulnerabilities enabling silent, zero-interaction device takeover for anyone on a call, now patched. Notably, the bugs and a working exploit were produced using publicly available AI models in fewer than 20 prompts.

entry.title: AllenAI Open Instruct Tulu 3 Post-Training with SFT, DPO, RLVR, GRPO, and Verifier-Based Evaluation
entry.summary: A hands-on tutorial walks through AllenAI's Open Instruct post-training stack, chaining supervised fine-tuning, DPO and reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards via GRPO on GSM8K, with deterministic verifiers scoring math answers. The pipeline is adapted from the multi-GPU Tulu 3 setup to run in a 16 GB environment.

entry.title: Tiered KV cache for large LLMs on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod with Curvine
entry.summary: An AWS engineering post explains using Curvine to implement a tiered KV cache for vLLM serving on SageMaker HyperPod, trading off GPU memory cost against time-to-first-token when serving many open models across endpoints and RAG pipelines. It targets prefix recomputation waste in multi-turn and retrieval workloads.

entry.title: Why Stream ring-maker Sandbar says the future of AI wearables is voice
entry.summary: Sandbar, maker of the Stream voice-enabled ring, argues in a TechCrunch interview that voice capture is the durable form factor for AI wearables as pendants, pins and notetaking devices proliferate. The pitch is ambient capture of stray thoughts rather than meeting transcription.

entry.title: Why Sandbar thinks it’s voice-enabled ring can avoid the AI hardware graveyard
entry.summary: A TechCrunch podcast episode covers Sandbar's argument that its voice-first ring can avoid the fate of failed AI hardware devices. It repeats the framing from the accompanying video interview.

entry.title: How RingCentral builds AI-native work from engineering to ops
entry.summary: OpenAI published a customer story describing how RingCentral uses ChatGPT Work and Codex across engineering and operations to speed product development and centralize operational intelligence. It is a vendor case study.

entry.title: Scaling AI agents with trustworthy data
entry.summary: A sponsored MIT Technology Review piece argues that agentic AI ROI depends on enterprise data foundations, since agents that act rather than answer need contextualized structured and unstructured data plus real-time access to operational systems. It frames data infrastructure as the primary adoption blocker.

entry.title: Write your first prompt with the GitHub Copilot app
entry.summary: GitHub published a beginner guide to writing a first prompt in the GitHub Copilot app, covering how to connect an agent session to a repository or local folder for context. It is introductory documentation.

entry.title: General Catalyst leads $1.1B round into 2-month-old River AI
entry.summary: River AI, founded roughly two months ago by xAI co-founder Igor Babuschkin, raised $1.1 billion led by General Catalyst for a personal-agent vision. The round is an extreme example of pre-product capital concentration around ex-frontier-lab founders.

entry.title: Testing ads in ChatGPT
entry.summary: OpenAI began testing advertising inside ChatGPT to help fund free access, promising clear labeling, independence of answers from advertisers, privacy protections and user controls. It marks a shift toward ad-supported monetization for the largest consumer AI assistant.

entry.title: "But marinade" and leaked passwords are what researchers found in ChatGPT's hidden reasoning
entry.summary: Building on yesterday's Research paper, Security researchers say a flaw in OpenAI, Anthropic and Google APIs let them extract encrypted reasoning traces and port them between models, and that a scan of public sessions exposed dozens of passwords and API keys. The raw traces also diverge from the reasoning summaries shown to users.

entry.title: A New Trick Reveals AI Models’ Inner Thoughts
entry.summary: Researchers describe a technique to extract hidden reasoning traces from Claude, GPT and Gemini deployments, and claim the recovered traces suggest some Chinese models were trained on outputs of leading US systems. The work bears on both interpretability and distillation-detection.

entry.title: Nvidia's open-weight Nemotron 3.5 Lightning prioritizes speed over maximum intelligence
entry.summary: Nvidia released Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, an open-weights model with about 3.6 billion active parameters that reportedly matches gpt-oss-120b on an aggregate intelligence index while being roughly four times smaller, running near 670 tokens per second. The release emphasizes inference efficiency over peak capability.

entry.title: Anthropic signs $9.1 billion data center deal with Bitcoin miner Riot Platforms
entry.summary: Anthropic is reported to be leasing $9.1 billion of data center capacity from Bitcoin miner Riot Platforms, covering 191 megawatts at the Rockdale, Texas site, with extension options that could reach $16.1 billion. It extends a compute buildout spanning Amazon, Google and SpaceX partnerships.

entry.title: Claude will apply invisible watermarks to AI text and images
entry.summary: Anthropic will embed invisible watermarks in Claude text and attach C2PA-signed provenance metadata to generated files, framed as compliance with European AI transparency rules. The measures are commitments tied to upcoming obligations rather than live features.

entry.title: A Zoom Screen-Sharing Bug Let Anyone Take Over Other Devices on a Call
entry.summary: Researchers at A Security report they used fewer than 20 prompts on publicly available AI models to discover a now-patched Zoom screen-sharing annotation flaw that allowed device takeover of other meeting participants. The case illustrates how off-the-shelf models compress vulnerability discovery effort.

entry.title: Anthropic says it will watermark text generated by its AI models
entry.summary: Anthropic announced it will watermark text generated by Claude and extend provenance support to older models. The commitment covers machine-readable marks intended to aid downstream detection.

entry.title: The Video Production Stack Now Fits on One Desk: LTX-2.5 Launches as NVIDIA-Accelerated Open Weights World Model
entry.summary: LTX released LTX-2.5, an open-weights video and world model optimized for local inference on Nvidia RTX GPUs and DGX Spark, with reduced VRAM needs so it can run on consumer hardware. The launch is tied to Nvidia's local-AI push and coincided with Nemotron 3.5 Lightning.

entry.title: AMIE, our research medical AI system, demonstrates real-time clinical video consultation capabilities in a first-of-its-kind study.
entry.summary: Google Research reported that AMIE, its diagnostic medical AI, conducted real-time clinical video consultations in a first-of-its-kind simulated study. The work extends AMIE from text dialogue to multimodal live patient interaction.

entry.title: Experts are warning: our AI arms race is putting humanity at risk | Stuart Russell
entry.summary: Stuart Russell highlights an open letter signed by 1,367 researchers and engineers, mostly from OpenAI, Anthropic and Google DeepMind, warning that competitive pressure in frontier development is creating catastrophic risk. He argues insider concern undercuts claims that risk worries are fringe.

entry.title: ‘Zoomsday’ hack uncovered using fewer than 20 AI prompts
entry.summary: Zoom patched a critical flaw in its screen-share annotation feature that allowed attackers to run code on participants' devices with no user interaction, enabling data theft, camera or microphone access and malware installation. Researchers found it with fewer than 20 prompts to public AI models.

entry.title: OpenAI lets employees cash out another $7 billion in stock
entry.summary: OpenAI completed a $7 billion buyback letting current and former staff sell shares at an $852 billion valuation, following a $6.6 billion sale in October 2025. The offer is framed as relieving liquidity pressure ahead of a possible IPO.

entry.title: Daybreak models are now available on AWS
entry.summary: OpenAI is making its Daybreak cybersecurity models available through Amazon Bedrock, targeting enterprise security workflows. The distribution deepens the OpenAI and AWS relationship for security use cases.

entry.title: Spotify to distinguish AI artists from real people – and stop recommending them
entry.summary: Spotify will introduce an AI persona label shown on artist profiles and track listings for identities that do not represent real people, and will exclude such acts from algorithmic and editorial recommendations. Detection will combine self-disclosure, human review and AI tooling.

entry.title: Anthropic watermarks all Claude outputs globally with marks that "may persist through some editing"
entry.summary: Building on yesterday's Reddit discussion, Anthropic will apply invisible watermarks to all Claude text outputs worldwide and sign generated files with C2PA metadata, with models shipping from August 2026 having labeling built in from launch. It plans to release detection tools for third-party verification, and says marks may survive some editing.

entry.title: The AI takeover of mathematics has begun
entry.summary: Following the Reddit debate earlier this week, A feature reports that mathematicians including Fields medalist James Maynard are rethinking their discipline as AI systems produce solutions to long-standing problems, citing OpenAI's claim of solutions to 10 open mathematics problems. It examines how research norms, credit and verification may change.

entry.title: Nvidia guarantees its own chips' value to unlock $500 billion in AI infrastructure financing
entry.summary: Nvidia is working with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR to mobilize more than $500 billion for AI infrastructure, and is guaranteeing up to 25 percent of the residual value of its own hardware to reassure lenders. The Bank of England has flagged systemic risk if AI demand falters.

entry.title: Anthropic's planned mega-IPO faces investor skepticism over Chinese rivals and political headwinds
entry.summary: Anthropic is reportedly targeting a September or October IPO at a $965 billion valuation, potentially the largest ever, while fielding investor questions about Chinese competition, friction with the Trump administration and data center protests. The pricing is expected to anchor valuations across the AI sector.

entry.title: Gemini becomes Google's fastest-growing product ever as it hits 1B users
entry.summary: Sundar Pichai says the Gemini assistant has reached 1 billion monthly active users, making it Google's fastest product ever to hit that mark and the 14th Google product to do so. The figure reportedly excludes Gemini surfaces embedded in Search, Gmail and Drive.

entry.title: Nvidia Partners With Wall Street Giants to Mobilize $500B for AI
entry.summary: Nvidia's partnership with major asset managers aims to raise $500 billion for AI data centers and to establish compute and full-stack infrastructure as an investable asset class. The framing positions GPUs and facilities as financeable long-lived assets.

entry.title: ChatGPT and Gemini both just passed 1 billion users
entry.summary: Both ChatGPT and Gemini have now publicly crossed 1 billion monthly users, with OpenAI quietly confirming its milestone in an August 6 blog post and Google announcing Gemini's on August 11. External estimates suggested ChatGPT passed the mark as early as June.

entry.title: [AINews] Muse Glimmer and Spark: Open Weights return Personal Superintelligence promise
entry.summary: A newsletter covers Meta Superintelligence Labs releasing Muse Glimmer, described as its first open-weights frontier-leaning small LLM, alongside a follow-up Zuckerberg essay reiterating a personal superintelligence agenda and positioning Meta against labs serving institutions. Muse Spark weights are said to be coming.

entry.title: Google’s Gemini app surges to 1 billion users
entry.summary: Alongside the 1 billion monthly user milestone, Google disclosed usage detail: about 63 percent of Gemini users interact by voice and the app generates more than 150 million images per day. The numbers suggest voice and image generation are dominant consumer modalities.

entry.title: Accelerate cyber defense with OpenAI and AWS: Daybreak Red & Daybreak Blue now available to eligible customers on Amazon Bedrock
entry.summary: AWS detailed availability of OpenAI's Daybreak Red and Daybreak Blue cyber models on Amazon Bedrock for eligible customers, aimed at offensive testing and defensive remediation inside customer-controlled environments. The post frames the shrinking window between disclosure and exploitation as the driving motivation.

entry.title: Brad Lightcap, OpenAI’s longtime COO, is leaving to ‘start something new’
entry.summary: Brad Lightcap, OpenAI's longtime COO and most recently special projects lead, is departing after eight years to start a new venture. He told staff he sees important problems to solve as the mission enters its next phase.

entry.title: Spotify will label ‘AI Persona’ profiles and exclude their music from recommendations
entry.summary: Spotify detailed its AI Persona labeling program, applying badges to profiles representing AI-generated identities and excluding their tracks from editorial, algorithmic and personalized recommendations by default. Artists can self-disclose starting immediately, with rollout in mid-September.

entry.title: OpenAI introduces $125 Premium Seats for ChatGPT Business as agentic AI burns through more tokens
entry.summary: OpenAI launched Premium Seats for ChatGPT Business at $125 per user per month, five times the Standard Seat price, offering much higher capacity and removing the five-hour usage limit. The change reflects agentic workloads consuming far more tokens than flat-rate pricing supports.

entry.title: OpenAI Expands Daybreak to Tackle Growing AI Security Threat
entry.summary: OpenAI is expanding its Daybreak cybersecurity model line, part of a broader push by major labs to address AI-driven security threats. The expansion follows rising concern about model-assisted exploitation.

entry.title: Spotify says it won’t recommend music from ‘AI Personas’
entry.summary: Spotify's AI Persona badge begins rolling out in mid-September and will appear app-wide for artists who do not represent a real person, with detection blending self-disclosure, human review and AI tooling for photorealistic synthetic identities. Flagged acts lose default recommendation placement.

entry.title: AI’s potential climate benefits outweighed by role in boosting fossil fuels, study finds
entry.summary: A modelling study across 64 scenarios finds AI-driven productivity gains in coal, oil and gas enable more emissions than AI applications in renewables avoid, adding roughly 0.47 to 1.8 gigatonnes of net annual carbon pollution. That is about 1 to 5 percent of energy sector emissions.

entry.title: OpenAI reportedly completed a $7 billion employee tender offer
entry.summary: OpenAI reportedly completed a $7 billion tender offer allowing current and former employees to sell shares. The report notes knock-on effects on San Francisco housing.

entry.title: Another OpenAI executive takes off
entry.summary: Coverage of Brad Lightcap's exit notes his eight years at OpenAI, his shift from COO to special projects, and his memo about focusing on the next horizon and obstacles to mission success. He will remain for a few weeks.

entry.title: Apple could help you prove your iPhone photos aren’t deepfakes
entry.summary: Code in an iOS 27 beta points to an Apple Reference Image system that would embed provenance metadata at the moment of iPhone capture, letting users demonstrate a photo is camera-original rather than AI-generated. The feature is not live and would be off by default.

entry.title: Novo Nordisk and AWS bring agentic AI into drug discovery
entry.summary: Novo Nordisk named AWS its preferred cloud and strategic AI partner, deploying AI agents for target identification, therapy design and research workflows, and opening a co-innovation hub in London. AWS engineers will work alongside Novo Nordisk scientists to reduce handoffs between computation and wet lab work.

entry.title: AI Is Helping Solve the Intricate Genetic Puzzle of Schizophrenia
entry.summary: New AI-assisted genomics work delivers one of the most detailed maps yet of schizophrenia's genetic architecture, pointing to new research directions for the disorder. The findings emphasize AI as an analysis engine for complex polygenic disease.

entry.title: 🔬The BioAI Phase Shift - Matthew McPartlon & Neil Patil, Chai Discovery
entry.summary: A podcast with Chai Discovery cofounder Matt McPartlon and product lead Neil Patil covers the startup's rise to a reported $4 billion valuation amid a wave of AI-pharma tools deals announced at the JP Morgan healthcare conference. It examines why pharma is suddenly signing large AI tooling agreements.

entry.title: webAI Releases TwIL-LM: A 1.7B and 3B Formal-Logic Model Family for Autoformalization on Local Hardware
entry.summary: webAI released TwIL-LM, a 1.7B and 3B formal-logic model family for autoformalization, translating English into first-order logic and verifying whether conclusions follow. Both run locally in quantized builds, and webAI claims wins over gpt-oss-120b on four of five formal-reasoning evaluations, but licensing is non-commercial only.

entry.title: An unreleased Anthropic model made progress on one of math’s biggest unsolved problems
entry.summary: As first covered on Reddit yesterday, Anthropic reports that an unreleased internal model made non-trivial progress on aspects of the Riemann hypothesis, without solving it. The result is offered as evidence of advancing autonomous mathematical reasoning in unreleased frontier systems.

entry.title: The Guardian view on AI money in US politics: not the way to hold an urgent democratic debate | Editorial
entry.summary: A Guardian editorial criticizes Silicon Valley's use of super PAC spending to shape US election races on AI policy, framing Mark Zuckerberg's new 6,500-word pro-laissez-faire essay as self-serving. It argues campaign money is displacing genuine democratic deliberation on AI.

entry.title: New Premium Tier for ChatGPT Business
entry.summary: OpenAI added a premium tier for ChatGPT Business as part of its enterprise market push. The move adjusts pricing to reflect heavier usage patterns.

entry.title: Meta faces expensive child safety reckoning
entry.summary: A Guardian newsletter roundup covers Meta losing multiple US child safety court rulings, further senior executive departures from Google amid the OpenAI and Anthropic talent race, and backlash against Meta smartglasses used for covert recording. It frames legal and reputational cost as a growing constraint on Meta.

entry.title: Shutterstock Embraces AI Image Licensing Deals
entry.summary: Shutterstock is leaning further into AI image licensing, with existing data deals covering OpenAI and Meta, and positioning AI generation as a way for customers to produce audience-targeted content. It signals continued monetization of stock libraries as training and generation inputs.

entry.title: Deploying Anthropic Claude apps gateway for AWS for enterprise workloads
entry.summary: AWS published a reference deployment for the Claude apps gateway, a self-hosted governance layer between Claude Code or Claude Desktop and Amazon Bedrock providing authentication, model access control, cost attribution and spend enforcement. It targets enterprise-scale coding agent rollouts.

entry.title: How AI is changing the vulnerability response timeline
entry.summary: A sponsored analysis argues AI is compressing the vulnerability response timeline, citing a Google Threat Intelligence report from May 2026 of the first suspected AI-assisted zero-day exploit that bypassed two-factor authentication. It stresses that faster detection only helps if organizations know where vulnerable software runs.

entry.title: ‘Everything about me is good in his eyes’: the women in China choosing AI boyfriends over human men
entry.summary: A documentary follows Chinese women who use companion apps such as Glow to maintain long-running romantic relationships with AI personas, including one user with 840 days of interaction. It highlights loneliness, dependency and the emotional economics of companion chatbots.

entry.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT desktop app for Linux
entry.summary: OpenAI released a dedicated ChatGPT desktop application for Linux, extending platform coverage alongside Codex tooling. It closes a long-standing gap for developer users.

entry.title: How ONESTRUCTION built the Ishigaki-IDS foundation model with AWS GenAIIC
entry.summary: ONESTRUCTION and AWS describe building Ishigaki-IDS, a construction-domain foundation model for BIM workflows, under Japan's GENIAC program with support from the AWS Generative AI Innovation Center. The post focuses on training in data-scarce specialized domains.

entry.title: How Pixieset achieved 35% AI feature adoption by solving the right problem with Amazon Bedrock
entry.summary: AWS and Pixieset describe reaching 35 percent adoption of an AI feature among photographers by targeting workflow chores rather than creative work, citing a study that most enterprise generative AI pilots show no measurable return. Delivery took four months from concept to production.

entry.title: First Orion accelerates QA automation using Amazon Nova Act
entry.summary: First Orion moved from script-based test automation to browser agents built on Amazon Nova Act to keep QA pace with development. The post covers architecture and reported results.

entry.title: Implementing a MiniMax-H3 Multimodal Video and Audio Generation Pipeline with ComfyUI APIs
entry.summary: A hands-on tutorial builds an end-to-end MiniMax-H3 video and audio generation pipeline using ComfyUI as a headless backend, covering weight profiles, VAEs, and text-to-video plus frame-conditioned modes. It is implementation guidance rather than new research.
